newsitem.title: USA: US wheat group opposed to USDA grain stock plan.
newsitem.headline: US wheat group opposed to USDA grain stock plan.

text.p: U.S. wheat growers on Thursday said they were opposed to using money from two U.S. Agriculture Department export programs to rebuild emergency grain reserves.

"This idea is a 'Trojan Horse'," National Association of Wheat Growers President Phil McLain said in a prepared statement. "Once stocks are rebuilt, they will overhang markets and be a threat to prices in the longer term."

Earlier this week, USDA aides briefed congressional staffers on the idea of taking funds from the Export Enhancement Program and the PL480 program to replenish two grains reserves which have been drawn down in recent years.

One is the Food Security Commodity Reserve, which is used to respond to international humanitarion disasters. The other reserve is used for domestic purposes, such as providing feed assistance to livestock producers in times of drought.
USDA should be using EEP and the PL480 to bolster U.S. wheat exports, which are 28 percent below last year's pace, instead of to refill the reserves, NAWG said.
U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Thursday that the idea is still in the discussion stage.
Ultimately, Congress would have to decide whether to change the law in that manner, he said.
